name: Git
version_context: Git object model and reference model
summary: A distributed version-control system built around immutable content-addressed objects and mutable references over commit history.

features.name: Content-addressed object storage
features.description: Blobs, trees, commits, and annotated tags are addressed by identifiers derived from their serialized content.
benefits: Supports structural sharing and integrity checks
costs: History rewriting creates new identities rather than editing existing commits

features.name: Mutable reference layer
features.description: Branches and tags provide names that point to objects while the referenced objects remain immutable.
benefits: Branch creation and movement are lightweight
costs: Reachability and retention depend on reference and reflog policy

mathematical_views.question: How can a snapshot refer to immutable nested content and detect changes?
assumptions: Hash collisions are treated as outside the modeled failure boundary

mathematical_views.question: How are commit ancestry and merge relationships represented?
assumptions: A newly created commit references existing parent commits
The model uses parent-to-child edges consistently

benefits: Immutable identity and efficient reuse of unchanged subtrees
costs: Changing commit metadata or parents changes the commit identity

benefits: Cheap branching and explicit history navigation
costs: Garbage collection and reflog expiry affect recovery boundaries

evidence.title: Git user manual: Git objects and references
evidence.notes: Primary documentation for the object model and content-addressed storage.
